# Pending changes (since patch 0018, 2026-11-22)
## 2026-11-22 - Lighter frames on planets: lazy far life, a longer economy tick, ground meshes paced on foot

Asked: "fix everything" (towns and pirate camps under 600 FPS).

Found with a profile of the engine itself (perf, Godot's debug symbols): on a planet's surface the main thread
is the limit (a quarter of the pixels runs no faster) - its scripts about two fifths of it, drawing a third.
Done:
- **Far life lazier**: townspeople and animals more than 35 m from you think a frame in three (the time they
  missed added in); the townspeople's animations too (posed a frame in three, by hand). Near ones every frame.
  An animal's hit flash set only while it shows.
- **The economy's tick 6 s, not 2** (its changes scaled by the tick, the drift of goods nobody makes or uses
  too): a third of the work a second. Its test simulates the same 400 s.
- **The ground on foot paced finer**: turning built patches into meshes 0.35 ms a frame on foot or slow (1.5 ms
  flying fast), the quadtree's visit 0.2 ms a slice - the same work over more frames.
- **The rocks near you looked up from a cache** that's no longer thrown away whenever any patch is built (while
  walking that was nearly every frame); the walker's own look-up cached too. The camera's ground check a sample
  every ~1.2 m along its line, not always ten.
- **The toolbar** redrawn only when what it shows changes (looked at 30 times a second); the HUD's "where you
  are" and "E: ..." looked up ten times a second, not every redraw.
- The itch page's hangar picture replaced by the port's bar.
Tried and dropped: a separate rendering thread (slower: 426 / 388 FPS).
Numbers (run alone): town 540 -> 583 FPS, pirate camp 530 -> 624; scripts on the main thread in town about
0.9 -> 0.45 ms a frame (walker 0.21 -> 0.08, townspeople 0.14 -> 0.07, animals 0.16 -> 0.07, economy 0.10 -> 0.03,
rocks 0.18 -> 0.01). The slowest 5% of frames on planets are still ~2.1-2.2 ms.

Files: scripts/world/life/cosmos_npc.gd, cosmos_creature.gd; scripts/sim/galaxy.gd; scripts/world/space/
cosmos.gd, cosmos_planet.gd; scripts/ui/toolbar.gd; scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd; tests/test_trade_goods.gd.

## 2026-11-22 - The sector's people: everyone tracked, their ships followed; landing square on the pad

Asked: "every npc tracked correctly: npcs do not spawn randomly on stations, they either work there or they land
with their ships, use the facilities and services and leave. I should be able to follow an npc back to his ship,
then follow his ship to another station and continue doing this. A real simulation of npc jobs, lives and
choices, npcs owning ships and houses, having family and friends, joining fleets and wars, participating in the
every day life of the empire and its economy"; "landing on a pad should be aligned to the pad: the nose to the
top side of the pad, the thrusters to the bottom side, no diagonal or weird angle landing, for every ship; the
landing HUD to illustrate this".

Done:
- **People** (new autoload, scripts/sim/people.gd): everyone in the sector as a record - name, family name, age,
  empire, home (a station, or a town and its house), job, where they work, money, ship, partner, children,
  parents, friends, a short log of their life. A new game peoples the sector (~3100: each station's staff -
  bartender, 2 harbour officers, 2 port guards, 2 dock workers, 2 cargo hands - and their households; each
  trader's captain, its owner, and 1-3 crew; each fleet's sailors - one a warship), a little a frame under the
  loading screen; a town's households made the first time you come near it (6 houses, 12 in a city).
- **Their lives go on**, a share of them a frame (each looked at every 20 s): they age (a year = 40 min of
  play), are paid, make friends of the people they work and live with, pair off with a friend (and move in),
  have children (rarer as the sector fills), grow up and find work (a vacancy at their station, a berth on a ship
  docked there, the navy at war), save up - a crew member with 9000 dr buys a ship of their own (a new trader
  in the economy) and captains it - enlist at war, die (of age; with their ship, when it's destroyed; with
  their fleet's losses, mourned at home); a captain's ship passes to the first mate. Saved with the galaxy
  (~870 KB, 36 ms).
- **Where they are follows from what they do**: a ship's people at the station while it's docked, aboard while
  it travels; staff on shift or off it (shifts of a third of a day). Kept current at every change (groups by
  ship, fleet and home - nothing ever counts everyone).
- **The economy's traders are the ships you see** (Cosmos): no random traders any more - each of Galaxy's
  traders in your system is flown (on its pad down the lift, or partway along its leg - from the gate it came in
  by or the station it left, to its destination or the gate it leaves by), lands, waits out its time in port,
  lifts off and flies on to its next stop, through the gates to the next system; leaving the system hands it
  back to the economy where it is. 200 traders in the sector (was 110).
- **The port's people are the sector's** (CosmosHangar): the staff of the station (on shift), its residents in
  the bar and the lounge, and the people of the ships down on this platform's lifts - they walk out of the
  ship's spot when it lands, about the port, and back aboard before it lifts off. Each has their own face,
  name and job; "Who are you?" tells their story (work, family, friends, lately). A town's street people are
  its residents too.
- **Following a ship**: the target view shows a trader's name, captain and crew, docked or bound for where.
- **Landing square on the pad** (every ship): the nose to the pad's top (toward the station), the engines to its
  bottom - set down only within 12 degrees of its axis; the NPC ships, the auto-dock and your ship lifted out of
  the port all line up with it. The pads are painted with their axis and a chevron at the top; the landing
  display shows the pad's top edge bold, its axis and chevron, your heading off it, "HEADING".
- **Frame rate**: "by the station" 464 -> 828 fps (the people's whereabouts no longer recounted every frame);
  the hangar's walking bounds 0.43 -> 0.05 ms a frame (its furniture by 6 m cells); a new game's map made a few
  systems a frame (a 32 ms loading frame gone); a system's traders built a few a frame.
- Tests: the traders flown are the economy's (docked, on legs, released on leaving); the port's people are the
  sector's (staff on shift, a ship's crew ashore while it's in port); manual docking requires the alignment.

Files: scripts/sim/people.gd (new), project.godot (autoload), scripts/sim/galaxy.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd,
scripts/world/space/cosmos_npc_ship.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos_station.gd, scripts/world/station/cosmos_hangar.gd,
scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_target_view.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd,
tests/test_trade_goods.gd; the guide (data/docs/game.md: landing square on the pad, the port's people, following a
trader), data/docs/shots.json (the pad shot: a heading note), the shots retaken.

## 2026-11-22 - No crash on closing the game

Asked (the game's window closed with a crash, twice, as it was closed): the crash was in Godot's shutdown - its
worker pool freeing background tasks never collected (wait_for_task_completion), whose calls belonged to scripts
already gone. The builds kept for the whole run - the empires' ship designs (EmpireHulls), your ship's hull and
its rooms, the 3D noise, the planets' maps - are started at the title and collected only when first used: one
never used stayed in the pool to the end. Now ProcArt, leaving, collects them all (EmpireHulls.finish,
CosmosShip / CosmosShipInterior / Cosmos / PlanetMapPage.finish_tasks). Every Godot run had crashed on exit
(hundreds of crash dumps from the tests a day); a full test run now leaves none, and the game closes cleanly.
Files: scripts/core/proc_art.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_ship.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_ship_interior.gd,
scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, scripts/ui/pages/planet_map_page.gd.

## 2026-11-22 - The free mouse: click to select, drag to steer, right click for actions

Asked: "ctrl + right click to release mouse focus; in this mode left click held down and dragging around acts as
the captured mouse, single left clicks select things and single right clicks open the right click menu for
actions like docking on stations"; "ctrl + right click again captures the mouse and goes back to the default
mode"; "make sure those shortcuts are customisable in settings too".
Done:
- **The free mouse** (Cosmos): Ctrl + right click frees the mouse (the cursor shown; kept from system to
  system); again: captured, as before. Free: a click (pressed and let go within 6 px) selects what's under the
  cursor - planet, station, gate, ship, monster, lair: the nearest to the cursor within its size on the screen
  (28 px at least) - as your target; held and dragged it steers the ship / turns your view on foot exactly as
  the captured mouse (CosmosShip / CosmosCam read the motion while Cosmos.mouse_steers()); never fires. A right
  click opens the actions menu (the game's theme) for what's under the cursor or your target: target it, ask a
  station for a pad / cancel the request, land on the planet below, take off / undock, get up from the seat or
  get out, the terminal beside you, take the pilot's seat, dismiss / recall your ship, capture the mouse.
- **Mouse buttons as bindings** (Keybinds): a new slot kind, "m:<modifiers+><button>" (Left, Right, Middle,
  Back, Forward - with Ctrl / Shift / Alt like a key's); three new actions in a "Mouse" group - free_mouse
  (Ctrl+Right), pointer (Left: select / drag), action_menu (Right) - rebindable in Settings > Controls, which
  now takes a mouse button in a key slot (shown "Ctrl+Right click").
- The guide's Controls: the free mouse.
Files: scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_ship.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_cam.gd,
scripts/core/keybinds.gd, scripts/ui/main_menu.gd, data/docs/game.md.

Done:
- **CosmosNpcInterior** (new): a trader down in a port can be walked into - up its stern ramp, through the door

  cross-section, sampled every 0.4 m), each slice's room as wide as the nearest skin at standing height leaves

  CUTAWAY define - a box of its own space not drawn, its corners instance parameters - worn only by ships

## 2026-11-22 - Riding the traders: across the system, through the gates; your ship left where you left it

Asked (playing): "when I board an npc ship, when it leaves the station it kicks me out of the ship - I want to
stay with the ship and it to take me with it to its destination"; asked which way for your own ship: "it stays
where you left it".
Done (Cosmos):
- **Aboard wherever it goes**: no more being walked off - you stay on its deck (carried with it) up its lift,
  across the system, to its next port; its door shut behind you while its ramp's up (the walls hold, the hull
  whole), open again when it's down. The port under the pad it goes down on opened as it goes down (its people,
  its rooms) - walk down its ramp into it. "Aboard the <ship> - <room>" / "Bound for <station>" or "the gate to
  <system>" in the panel. Its ship destroyed with you aboard: you're downed.
- **Through the gates**: aboard when it reaches its gate, the next system is built (under the veil) and you're
  aboard it there, coming in from that system's gate, on its way to its next stop.
- **Your ship stays where you left it**: docked at the station you rode away from - in another system it isn't
  built at all (nothing of it shown); the panel in a port without it says where it is ("Your ship: at Nyx
  Relay, Knossos - B: recall it").
- **Recalled** (B in a port your ship isn't in): it comes to you - 20 s + the way across the system, or 40 s +
  45 s a jump from another system - waits for a free pad of your port ("waiting for a free pad") and comes down
  its lift (the docking lift), docked there; its old pad freed.
- **Saved and loaded**: not aboard a moving ship (the Esc menu's Save and the autosaves wait); on foot in a port
  your ship isn't in, the save keeps where you are and where your ship is - loaded, you're on foot in that port
  and your ship where you left it (in another system: away; in this one: docked at its pad). The station
  services, missions and the port's people are the station's whose port you're in.
- The guide: riding the traders, your ship left behind and recalled. A test: a save in a port with your ship in
  another system loads so, and the recall brings it down the port's lift.
Files: scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos_npc_interior.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd,
scripts/world/game/cosmos_game.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd, data/docs/game.md.

## 2026-11-22 - 3D solar map and galaxy map; the galaxy grown to 120 systems in 3D
Asked: "update our solar map and galaxy map. Solar map now is completely 3d with rotation, panning and zooming,
plotting course and detailed info panels about selected objects. Galaxy map is very similar, the available systems
are now 120 but like solar map there is a fog of war so only the visited solar systems are visible, galaxy map is
also 3d with similar navigation controls, make sure the solar systems are distributed all over its 3d space, again
panel with info for selected object and a course planner."
Done:
- Galaxy (scripts/sim/galaxy.gd): grown in two rounds - the old flat map's (FIRST_GROWTH: its 58 systems, ids and
  lanes kept), then every system given a height (pos3; "pos" stays its view from above) and grown on through a
  1350 x 700 x 1080 ellipsoid to 120 (EMPIRE_SIZE: Minoa 18, Athens 18, Sparta 17, Mycenae 16, Ionia 18, Cyclades 16;
  PIRATE_DENS 17). New lanes keep clear of other systems and lanes, up to 6 gates a system, 1-2 extra lanes each for
  loops. 192 lanes, all connected, max 11 jumps from Knossos, longest 321. Heights -686..643. New real place names,
  none repeated. Gates turned aside where two would overlap (gate_angles).
- Baked: data/galaxy.json (growing is ~0.5 s; reading 1.7 ms - the old 2D growth was 273 ms at every start);
  tools/bake_galaxy.gd re-bakes; test_maps fails when stale.
- Fog of war for the galaxy: Galaxy.been (systems you've been in, Knossos always; saved; old saves from their
  fog/charts/reports); current_system's setter marks it and moves the route on (follow_route); find_known_route
  (only through visited systems); is_known (visited or next to one). neighbors() cached.
- Map3DView + MapKit (scripts/ui/maps/), shaders/maps/ (5): a 3D map in a SubViewport, eased orbit camera; drag
  turn, right/middle drag pan, wheel zoom to cursor, click select, double click fly to, middle click/Home fit;
  keys/pad: WASD/arrows/D-pad/left stick turn, right stick pan, +/-/PgUp/PgDn/triggers zoom, Enter/A plot,
  Backspace/X next.
- Solar map (map_page.gd): star, worlds/moons on orbits, stations, gates, asteroid fields, bio-signatures, ships in
  sensor range, you - on stems over a 10 km polar grid; fog; details panel; Set course (your target), Clear course;
  list of everything known.
- Galaxy map (galaxy_page.gd): visited systems only, lanes between them, fading stubs to uncharted "?" neighbours;
  territories, war fronts, crisis arcs, your system's pulse; details (owner, star, worlds, state, pirates, stations
  known, visited, standing, wars, jumps + light-years, route); Plot/Clear route, Add waypoint (Shift+click), trade
  layer kept. CosmosMapMirror targets the next gate on arrival and sweeps the system fog round your ship.
- CosmosWarm draws the map shaders at the title; fps_tour: "the solar map open", "the galaxy map open" (~6% under

Numbers: 120 systems (18/18/17/16/18/16 + 17 dens), 192 lanes, height spread 1330, start-up galaxy 273 ms -> 1.7 ms,
5 shaders, overlay ~1-1.5 ms a redraw (4-8 Hz at rest), maps ~0.1 ms a frame.

## 2026-11-22/23 - A sandbox: start on foot, make a living, the interactive tutorial; a passenger seat

Asked: a passenger seat by the captain's chair of the ships you ride - sitting there, an outside view of the ship
you can turn and zoom (no control of it); "the player now starts on a green planet of the minoan system. All main
quests are completely removed, the game will be a complete sandbox"; an interactive tutorial (navigation, the maps,
the jet pack, mining); a city's miner vendor buying raw materials; starting gear - a pulse laser, a mining laser
and a scanner for veins and nearby places (caves, cities, enemies); a transport mission giver (a package carried,
with a carry animation, set down on the ground); a local pilot to rent a ride to the destination (a city on another
planet or a station); a few dozen missions for a first ship; the tutorial on step by step, rewarding toward the
first ship, then flying, docking and undocking, fighting pirates for bounties handed in at stations; persistent
in saves, never disruptive; another way to a first ship ends it once you've flown, docked and fought, with all its
rewards.
Done:
- **The passenger seat** (CosmosNpcInterior: a second chair beside the pilot's, where the bridge is wide enough):
  E there - the camera outside the ship (CosmosCam on it, its zoom sized to the ship, right drag to turn, the wheel
  to zoom); moving or E gets you up, your own eyes again.
- **A new game starts on foot on Amnissos** (the green ocean world of Knossos) by its first city's landing field,
  with no ship (CosmosGame.start_on_foot from the title's New game; extra no_ship) - your rifle, mining beam and the
  new scanner. The ship's not built until you have one; the panel says so ("You have no ship yet - a station's
  shipyard sells them"); B says how to get about; downed, you're back by the nearest town's field. Saved on foot on
  a world (extra on_planet) or in a port: loaded there.
- **No main quest**: Kilon Alios no longer stands by the cities' fields (CosmosSandbox's three in his place); the
  Ship Computer's Quest tab hidden; the encyclopedia's lore open; the guide's quest section replaced.
- **CosmosSandbox** (new): every city's **ore buyer** (your pack's raw ore, 1.5x its value), **courier's office**
  (three packages at a time for towns on the system's other worlds and its stations, ~300-480 dr each; carried in
  both hands - no rifle, no running; H sets it down / picks it up; handed over at the town's courier's office or the
  station's harbour office - its officer, or its Missions terminal, which also opens the missions board) and
  **local pilot** (a ride for 25-140 dr: their ship comes down on the field, you walk up its ramp, it climbs, swings
  round the world, crosses the system and comes down by the other world's town - or onto a station's pad, down into
  its port - you walk off). **The scanner** (Z, on foot): a pulse; the deposits within 600 m and the places within
  14 km - towns, caves and dungeons, pirate camps, lairs, armed creatures - marked on the HUD for a minute with names
  and distances. **Bounty vouchers**: a raider destroyed earns one (no longer paid at once), handed in at a
  harbour office.
- **The hired ride** (CosmosNpcShip.hire_ride: arrive, wait, climb, out, transfer, in, descend, landed, leave - its
  flight in the planets' own frames, smooth); boarding and leaving on a world's ground (Cosmos._npc_boarding).
- **Your first ship**: bought at a station's shipyard with none (trade-in 0, "You have no ship yet"), it comes down
  that port's lift onto a pad (the recall's arrival); the tutorial's ship step paid.
- **The carried package** (CosmosWalker: set_carry, hands(put_down / pick_up) - the new clips, the box let go at
  0.733 s, taken at 0.6 s; carry / carry_idle while holding it).
- **CosmosTutor** (new): a small panel top right (F2 hides it) - 17 steps, each done in any order and paid when
  done (40-300 dr; 1,500 for the first ship; 3,090 in all): walk, jet pack, maps, scanner, mine, sell ore, take a
  package, set it down / pick it up, a ride, deliver, your first ship; take the controls, undock, the Hyperion drive,
  dock (only after undocking), two raiders, hand in their bounties. A ship got before the first part's done: it
  ends once you've undocked, docked and fought, paying everything it would have. In the save (extra tutor); old
  saves have none.
- **Fixed on the way**: jumping at high frame rates (the ground's 2 cm snap caught a jump's first frames above ~300
  fps - you couldn't leave the ground); the jump key read only while carrying (my edit's order); the camera's
  frozen view when a cached solid part had gone.
- Tests: tests/test_tutor.gd (5: the start, steps paid one at a time, docking after undocking, followed to the end,
  ended another way with every reward, the pay adds up to a first ship in a few dozen deliveries); test_cosmos (the
  town's three people, the ore buyer's talk, bounty vouchers). Played through live end to end: new game, every step,
  the ride to Kephala Outpost, delivery, the ship bought, undocking, the drive, docking, two raiders, the vouchers.
- The guide: the start, Making a living, The tutorial (new shot space3d_start), the town section, the Ship Computer.
